class EmptyTruncatedReplyMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):
    """Fail the main run when the provider cut off a reply before any output.

    Without this, a reply with no text, no tool calls, and a truncation stop
    reason ends the run as a success. The empty message is checkpointed and
    the UI shows nothing, so the app looks hung. Raising instead fails the
    model node, so the empty message is not saved and the client shows the
    error. A partial reply is left alone; the client warns about it.

    This middleware never retries. It must wrap the retry middleware, so the
    error is not retried, and any recovery middleware that may still repair
    the reply.
    """

    trace_policy = TracePolicy(process_inputs=omit_payload)
    """Omit hook inputs from traces by default; set a `TracePolicy` to override."""

    @staticmethod
    def _check(response: ModelResponse, request: ModelRequest) -> None:
        if request.state.get(_FORKED_CONTEXT_KEY):
            return
        EmptyTruncatedReplyMiddleware._check_empty(response, request)

    @staticmethod
    def _check_empty(response: ModelResponse, request: ModelRequest) -> None:
        message = _final_ai_message(response)
        if message is None or has_visible_reply(message):
            return
        truncation = output_truncation(message)
        if truncation is None:
            return
        error = ModelOutputTruncatedError(
            truncation,
            _model_name(message, request.model),
            no_usage=_reported_no_usage(message),
            has_reasoning=any(
                block.get("type") == "reasoning" for block in message.content_blocks
            ),
            invalid_tool_call=bool(message.invalid_tool_calls),
        )
        logger.warning("%s", error)
        raise error

    @override
    def wrap_tool_call(
        self,
        request: ToolCallRequest,
        handler: Callable[[ToolCallRequest], ToolMessage | Command],
    ) -> ToolMessage | Command:
        """Return truncated subagent failures to the parent.

        Raises:
            ModelOutputTruncatedError: If a tool other than `task` raised it.
        """
        try:
            return handler(request)
        except ModelOutputTruncatedError as error:
            if request.tool_call["name"] != "task":
                raise
            return ToolMessage(
                str(error), tool_call_id=request.tool_call["id"], status="error"
            )

    @override
    async def awrap_tool_call(
        self,
        request: ToolCallRequest,
        handler: Callable[[ToolCallRequest], Awaitable[ToolMessage | Command]],
    ) -> ToolMessage | Command:
        """Return truncated subagent failures to the parent.

        Raises:
            ModelOutputTruncatedError: If a tool other than `task` raised it.
        """
        try:
            return await handler(request)
        except ModelOutputTruncatedError as error:
            if request.tool_call["name"] != "task":
                raise
            return ToolMessage(
                str(error), tool_call_id=request.tool_call["id"], status="error"
            )

    def wrap_model_call(
        self,
        request: ModelRequest,
        handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], ModelResponse],
    ) -> ModelResponse:
        """Raise when the reply was cut off before any output.

        Returns:
            The unchanged model response.
        """
        response = handler(request)
        self._check(response, request)
        return response

    async def awrap_model_call(
        self,
        request: ModelRequest,
        handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], Awaitable[ModelResponse]],
    ) -> ModelResponse:
        """Raise when the reply was cut off before any output.

        Returns:
            The unchanged model response.
        """
        response = await handler(request)
        self._check(response, request)
        return response


class SubagentTruncatedReplyMiddleware(EmptyTruncatedReplyMiddleware):
    """Keep partial subagent answers and fail empty ones for the parent to handle."""

    @property
    @override
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Replace the inherited parent guard in place when merging fork middleware."""
        return EmptyTruncatedReplyMiddleware.__name__

    @staticmethod
    def _check(response: ModelResponse, request: ModelRequest) -> None:
        EmptyTruncatedReplyMiddleware._check_empty(response, request)
        message = _final_ai_message(response)
        if message is None or message.tool_calls:
            return
        truncation = output_truncation(message)
        if truncation is None:
            return
        warning = f"Subagent reply was cut off: {describe_truncation(truncation)}."
        content = (
            f"{message.content}\n\n{warning}"
            if isinstance(message.content, str)
            else [*message.content, {"type": "text", "text": f"\n\n{warning}"}]
        )
        replacement = message.model_copy(update={"content": content})
        response.result = [
            replacement if item is message else item for item in response.result
        ]

r"""Large paste collapsing for the chat input.

When the user pastes text exceeding a size or line threshold, the full text
is stored off-screen and a compact `[Pasted text #N +M lines]` placeholder
is inserted into the input box instead.  At submission time the placeholder
is expanded back to the original content so the agent receives the full text.

This mirrors the behavior of Claude Code's paste-collapsing system.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

PASTE_THRESHOLD_CHARS = 800
"""Minimum character count for a paste to be collapsed into a placeholder."""

PASTE_THRESHOLD_LINES = 2
"""Minimum line count (newline-separated) for a paste to be collapsed."""

PASTE_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\[Pasted text #(\d+)(?: \+(\d+) lines)?\]")
"""Regex matching `[Pasted text #N]` or `[Pasted text #N +M lines]`."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PastedContent:
    """Stored content for a collapsed paste.

    The paste's numeric identifier is the key under which this record is
    stored in the input's paste map, so it is not duplicated on the record.

    Attributes:
        content: The full pasted text.
    """

    content: str


def count_lines(text: str) -> int:
    r"""Return the number of newline characters in `text`.

    Args:
        text: The text to count newlines in.

    Returns:
        The number of `\n` occurrences (0 for single-line text).
    """
    return text.count("\n")


def should_collapse_paste(text: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether `text` should be collapsed into a placeholder.

    Collapses when the text exceeds the character threshold or the line
    threshold.

    Args:
        text: The pasted text to evaluate.

    Returns:
        `True` if the paste should be collapsed.
    """
    return (
        len(text) > PASTE_THRESHOLD_CHARS or count_lines(text) > PASTE_THRESHOLD_LINES
    )


def format_paste_ref(paste_id: int, num_lines: int) -> str:
    """Format a paste placeholder reference string.

    Args:
        paste_id: The numeric paste identifier.
        num_lines: The number of extra lines (newlines) in the pasted content.

    Returns:
        `[Pasted text #N]` when `num_lines` is 0, otherwise
        `[Pasted text #N +M lines]`.
    """
    if num_lines == 0:
        return f"[Pasted text #{paste_id}]"
    return f"[Pasted text #{paste_id} +{num_lines} lines]"


def expand_paste_refs(text: str, pasted_contents: dict[int, PastedContent]) -> str:
    """Replace all paste placeholders in `text` with their full content.

    Placeholders whose IDs are not in `pasted_contents` are left unchanged.

    Args:
        text: The text containing placeholders.
        pasted_contents: Mapping of paste IDs to stored content.

    Returns:
        The text with all known placeholders expanded.
    """

    def _replace(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        content = pasted_contents.get(int(match.group(1)))
        # Return the stored text literally; unknown IDs keep their placeholder.
        return content.content if content is not None else match.group(0)

    return PASTE_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERN.sub(_replace, text)

"""Adapter from plugin hook declarations to Hooks v2 configuration sources."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from deepagents_code.hooks.loading import PluginHooksSource, read_hooks_json
from deepagents_code.hooks.models.domain import HookDiagnostic, HookEvent
from deepagents_code.plugins.manifest import find_manifest_path
from deepagents_code.plugins.substitution import plugin_environment

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pathlib import Path

    from deepagents_code.plugins.models import JsonValue, PluginInstance

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_KNOWN_EVENTS = frozenset(event.value for event in HookEvent)

PluginHooksDocument = tuple[PluginHooksSource, "JsonValue"]
PluginHookSources = tuple[tuple[PluginHooksDocument, ...], tuple[HookDiagnostic, ...]]


def _diagnostic(
    message: str, *, field: str | None = None, exc_info: bool = False
) -> HookDiagnostic:
    logger.warning(message, exc_info=exc_info)
    return HookDiagnostic(
        code="plugin_hooks_failed",
        severity="warning",
        message=message,
        field=field,
    )


def _plugin_documents(
    plugin: PluginInstance,
) -> tuple[list[tuple[Path, JsonValue]], list[HookDiagnostic]]:
    """Collect decoded file and inline hook documents in declaration order.

    Returns:
        Documents with diagnostic locations, plus read diagnostics.
    """
    documents: list[tuple[Path, JsonValue]] = []
    diagnostics: list[HookDiagnostic] = []
    for path in plugin.inventory.hook_files:
        decoded, document, read_diagnostics, _fingerprint = read_hooks_json(path)
        diagnostics.extend(read_diagnostics)
        if decoded:
            documents.append((path, document))
    manifest = plugin.manifest
    if manifest and manifest.inline_hooks:
        manifest_path = find_manifest_path(plugin.root) or plugin.root
        documents.append((manifest_path, manifest.inline_hooks))
    return documents, diagnostics


def discover_plugin_hook_sources(
    *,
    project_dir: Path | None = None,
    plugins: tuple[PluginInstance, ...] | None = None,
) -> PluginHookSources:
    """Build hook sources from enabled or already-discovered plugins.

    Args:
        project_dir: Project directory exposed as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`.
        plugins: Already-discovered plugins, or `None` to discover them here.

    Returns:
        Sourced hook documents and collection diagnostics.
    """
    diagnostics: list[HookDiagnostic] = []
    if plugins is None:
        try:
            from deepagents_code.plugins import discover_plugins

            result = discover_plugins()
        # Discovery failure must not take user and project hooks down with it.
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return (), (
                _diagnostic(f"Could not discover plugin hooks: {exc}", exc_info=True),
            )
        plugins = result.plugins
        diagnostics.extend(
            _diagnostic(f"Plugin discovery warning: {warning}")
            for warning in result.warnings
        )
    documents: list[PluginHooksDocument] = []
    for plugin in plugins:
        try:
            plugin_documents, plugin_diagnostics = _plugin_documents(plugin)
            if not plugin_documents:
                diagnostics.extend(plugin_diagnostics)
                continue
            try:
                plugin.data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            except OSError as exc:
                plugin_diagnostics.append(
                    _diagnostic(
                        f"Could not create the data directory for plugin "
                        f"{plugin.plugin_id}: {exc}",
                        field=str(plugin.data_dir),
                    )
                )
            env = plugin_environment(
                plugin_root=plugin.root,
                plugin_data=plugin.data_dir,
                project_dir=project_dir,
            )
            sources = tuple(
                (
                    PluginHooksSource(
                        location=str(path), plugin_id=plugin.plugin_id, env=env
                    ),
                    document,
                )
                for path, document in plugin_documents
            )
        # A broken plugin must not withhold every other plugin's hooks.
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            diagnostics.append(
                _diagnostic(
                    f"Could not load hooks for plugin {plugin.plugin_id}: {exc}",
                    field=str(plugin.root),
                    exc_info=True,
                )
            )
            continue
        documents.extend(sources)
        diagnostics.extend(plugin_diagnostics)
    return tuple(documents), tuple(diagnostics)


def plugin_hook_event_names(plugin: PluginInstance) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """List the hook events a plugin declares, for display before it loads.

    Only events Hooks v2 recognizes are returned, so the plugin manager never
    advertises a hook that the loader will later reject.

    Args:
        plugin: Plugin whose declarations should be inspected.

    Returns:
        Declared event names in declaration order, deduplicated.
    """
    events: list[str] = []
    documents, _diagnostics = _plugin_documents(plugin)
    for _path, document in documents:
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            continue
        hooks = document.get("hooks")
        if not isinstance(hooks, dict):
            continue
        events.extend(name for name in hooks if name in _KNOWN_EVENTS)
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(events))

"""Adapter from discovered plugins to `SkillsMiddleware` sources."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from deepagents_code.plugins.models import BrokenPluginInstall, PluginInstance

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Documentation aliases: these name the role each `str` plays in the source
# tuples below, but they are plain aliases, not `NewType`s. Any `str` satisfies
# all three, so swapping a label for a namespace still type-checks.
type SkillPath = str
type SkillLabel = str
type SkillNamespace = str
type DirectorySkillSource = tuple[SkillPath, SkillLabel]
type PluginSkillSource = tuple[SkillPath, SkillLabel, SkillNamespace]
type CodeSkillSource = DirectorySkillSource | PluginSkillSource


def namespaced_skill_name(
    namespace: SkillNamespace,
    name: str,
    subfolders: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> str:
    """Qualify a skill name under its plugin namespace.

    Nested skill directories contribute intermediate `:`-joined segments
    between the plugin namespace and the skill name, matching the plugin skill
    naming convention (e.g. `plugin:sub:review`).

    Args:
        namespace: Plugin namespace (its `plugin_id`).
        name: Skill name from the skill's frontmatter.
        subfolders: Directory names between the plugin skills root and the
            skill directory, in path order.

    Returns:
        The qualified skill name.
    """
    return ":".join((namespace, *subfolders, name)).lower()


def plugin_skill_sources(
    plugins: tuple[PluginInstance, ...],
) -> list[PluginSkillSource]:
    """Return skill source tuples for plugin skills.

    Args:
        plugins: Plugin instances.

    Returns:
        Source tuples containing path, label, and plugin namespace.
    """
    sources: list[PluginSkillSource] = []
    for plugin in plugins:
        for path in plugin.inventory.skills:
            source_path = path.parent if path.name == "SKILL.md" else path
            try:
                if not source_path.exists():
                    continue
            except OSError:
                logger.warning("Could not inspect plugin skill path %s", source_path)
                continue
            sources.append(
                (
                    str(source_path),
                    f"Plugin: {plugin.plugin_id}",
                    plugin.plugin_id,
                )
            )
    return sources


def plugin_skill_roots(plugins: tuple[PluginInstance, ...]) -> list[Path]:
    """Return plugin skill roots for skill-content containment checks.

    Args:
        plugins: Discovered plugin instances.

    Returns:
        Skill root directories.
    """
    roots: list[Path] = []
    for plugin in plugins:
        roots.extend(
            path.parent if path.name == "SKILL.md" else path
            for path in plugin.inventory.skills
        )
    return roots


def discover_plugin_skill_state() -> tuple[
    tuple[tuple[Path, str], ...],
    tuple[Path, ...],
    frozenset[str],
    tuple[BrokenPluginInstall, ...],
]:
    """Discover plugin skill sources, containment roots, loaded ids, and repairs.

    Returns:
        Plugin skill sources, roots, ids, and enabled plugins whose installed
        files are missing, or empty values when discovery fails.
    """
    plugin_sources: tuple[tuple[Path, str], ...] = ()
    plugin_roots: tuple[Path, ...] = ()
    plugin_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    try:
        from deepagents_code.plugins import discover_plugins

        result = discover_plugins()
        plugins = result.plugins
        plugin_sources = tuple(
            (Path(path), namespace)
            for path, _label, namespace in plugin_skill_sources(plugins)
        )
        plugin_roots = tuple(plugin_skill_roots(plugins))
        plugin_ids = frozenset(plugin.plugin_id for plugin in plugins)
    except OSError, RuntimeError:
        logger.warning("Could not discover plugin skills", exc_info=True)
        return (), (), frozenset(), ()

    return plugin_sources, plugin_roots, plugin_ids, result.broken


def discover_plugin_skill_sources_and_roots() -> tuple[
    tuple[tuple[Path, str], ...], tuple[Path, ...]
]:
    """Discover plugin skill sources and containment roots.

    Returns:
        Plugin skill sources and roots, or empty tuples when discovery fails.
    """
    plugin_sources, plugin_roots, _plugin_ids, _broken = discover_plugin_skill_state()

    return plugin_sources, plugin_roots

"""Code-local skills middleware adapter for plugin namespaces."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import uuid
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated, NotRequired, cast

from deepagents.backends.protocol import FileInfo, LsResult
from deepagents.backends.utils import to_posix_path
from deepagents.middleware import skills as sdk_skills
from deepagents.middleware.skills import SkillsMiddleware
from langchain.agents.middleware.types import OmitFromOutput
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from langgraph.config import get_stream_writer
from langgraph.types import Overwrite, interrupt

from deepagents_code.goal_state_notice import (
    GOAL_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SOURCE,
    is_internal_message,
    message_source,
)
from deepagents_code.plugins.adapters.skills import (
    CodeSkillSource,
    SkillNamespace,
    namespaced_skill_name,
)
from deepagents_code.skills.invocation import extra_skill_roots, pinned_skill_body
from deepagents_code.skills.load import load_skill_content
from deepagents_code.skills.load_errors import skills_load_errors_event
from deepagents_code.skills.merge import merge_skill
from deepagents_code.skills.trust import (
    SKILL_TRUST_INTERRUPT_TYPE,
    SkillTrustRequest,
    trust_skill_dir,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence

    from deepagents.backends.protocol import BackendProtocol
    from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
    from langchain_core.tools import BaseTool
    from langgraph.runtime import Runtime

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_PLUGIN_SKILL_SOURCE_LENGTH = 3
_SKILL_FILE = "SKILL.md"

_PROCESS_ID = uuid.uuid4().hex
"""Random ID of this process, recorded with each skill load.

A thread's skills were loaded by an earlier process when its recorded ID
differs. `/reload` restarts the agent server, so every thread rescans its skill
sources on its next turn.
"""


class _PluginSkillsState(sdk_skills.SkillsState):
    """SDK skills state plus the process that loaded `skills_metadata`."""

    skills_loaded_by: NotRequired[Annotated[str, OmitFromOutput]]
    """`_PROCESS_ID` of the process whose scan wrote `skills_metadata`.

    Not private, so a forked subagent inherits it with `skills_metadata` and
    does not rescan.
    """


class _SkillsStateUpdate(sdk_skills.SkillsStateUpdate, total=False):
    """SDK skills update that can also replace the pending `pinned_skills`."""

    pinned_skills: Overwrite
    skills_loaded_by: str


def _skill_invocation(state: sdk_skills.SkillsState) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return the `__skill` marker of the newest visible human message.

    Stops at that message, so an older turn's selection never applies. A goal
    continuation is hidden but starts its own turn, so it also stops the search.
    """
    for message in reversed(state.get("messages", [])):
        if not isinstance(message, HumanMessage):
            continue
        if message_source(message) == GOAL_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SOURCE:
            return {}
        if not is_internal_message(message):
            marker = message.additional_kwargs.get("__skill")
            return marker if isinstance(marker, dict) else {}
    return {}


def _pending_pin_update(state: sdk_skills.SkillsState) -> Overwrite | None:
    """Return an update retaining only the current turn's explicit selection.

    The SDK `pinned_skills` reducer appends any requested name. Only the name
    from this turn's trust-checked `/skill:` invocation may be pinned, and a pin
    left over from a failed turn is dropped.
    """
    names = state.get("pinned_skills") or []
    name = _skill_invocation(state).get("name")
    selected = [name] if isinstance(name, str) and name in names else []
    return Overwrite(selected) if selected != names else None


def _loaded_here(state: Mapping[str, object]) -> bool:
    """Return whether this process wrote the loaded `skills_metadata`.

    Reads `state` as a mapping because the SDK hooks type it as `SkillsState`,
    which lacks the `_PluginSkillsState` key.
    """
    return state.get("skills_loaded_by") == _PROCESS_ID


def _needs_load(state: sdk_skills.SkillsState) -> bool:
    """Return whether `before_agent` must scan the skill sources.

    Metadata loaded by an earlier process can be stale (see `_PROCESS_ID`).
    Current metadata serves a pending pin when it lists the selected skill.
    Otherwise the skill may have been added since the load.
    """
    loaded = state.get("skills_metadata")
    if loaded is None or not _loaded_here(state):
        return True
    name = _skill_invocation(state).get("name")
    if name not in (state.get("pinned_skills") or []):
        # No pin survives this turn, so the loaded metadata is enough.
        return False
    return all(skill["name"] != name for skill in loaded)


def _loaded_update(state: sdk_skills.SkillsState) -> _SkillsStateUpdate | None:
    """Return the pin trim for a turn that keeps the loaded metadata.

    Returns:
        An update replacing `pinned_skills`, or `None` when nothing changes.
    """
    pins = _pending_pin_update(state)
    if pins is None:
        return None
    return _SkillsStateUpdate(
        skills_metadata=state.get("skills_metadata") or [], pinned_skills=pins
    )


def _trusted_directory(skill: sdk_skills.SkillMetadata, denied: str) -> str:
    """Ask the user to trust the skill's resolved directory, then save it.

    `interrupt` returns the client's answer when the run resumes, so the
    calling node runs again from the start with the same skill.

    Args:
        skill: Skill whose `SKILL.md` resolves outside the trusted roots.
        denied: Containment error to report if the user does not approve.

    Returns:
        The approved directory, which is now in the trust store.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The path cannot be resolved, the user denied trust, or
            the approval could not be saved.
    """
    name = skill["name"]
    try:
        directory = str(Path(skill["path"]).resolve().parent)
    except (OSError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        raise ValueError(denied) from exc
    answer = interrupt(
        SkillTrustRequest(
            type=SKILL_TRUST_INTERRUPT_TYPE, skill=name, directory=directory
        )
    )
    if not isinstance(answer, dict) or answer.get("approved") is not True:
        raise ValueError(denied)
    if not trust_skill_dir(directory):
        msg = (
            f"Could not save trust for {directory}, so skill '{name}' cannot "
            "run. Check that the state directory is writable, or add the "
            "directory to [skills].extra_allowed_dirs."
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return directory


def _entries(
    ls_result: object, path: str, errors: list[str] | None = None
) -> list[FileInfo]:
    """Normalize a backend `ls` result to a list of entry dicts.

    Appends a listing error for `path` to `errors`, in the SDK's format for
    skill source errors.

    Returns:
        The listing entries, or an empty list when the result is empty or an
        unexpected shape.
    """
    if isinstance(ls_result, LsResult):
        if ls_result.error and errors is not None:
            errors.append(sdk_skills._format_skills_source_error(path, ls_result.error))
        return list(ls_result.entries or [])
    if isinstance(ls_result, list):
        return cast("list[FileInfo]", ls_result)
    return []


def _child_dirs(entries: list[FileInfo], root: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return `(name, path)` for each immediate subdirectory in `entries`.

    Returns:
        Name/path pairs for each immediate subdirectory, excluding `root`.
    """
    root_posix = PurePosixPath(to_posix_path(root))
    dirs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for entry in entries:
        if not entry.get("is_dir"):
            continue
        path = entry["path"]
        name = PurePosixPath(to_posix_path(path)).name
        # Skip the source dir itself if a backend echoes it back.
        if PurePosixPath(to_posix_path(path)) == root_posix:
            continue
        dirs.append((name, path))
    return dirs


def _has_skill_file(entries: list[FileInfo], root: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether `entries` contains a `SKILL.md` directly under `root`."""
    root_posix = PurePosixPath(to_posix_path(root))
    for entry in entries:
        path = PurePosixPath(to_posix_path(entry["path"]))
        if path.name == _SKILL_FILE and path.parent == root_posix:
            return True
    return False


def _missing(path: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether `path` does not exist, so its listing error is expected."""
    try:
        return not Path(path).exists()
    except OSError:
        # Cannot be checked, for example a parent without search permission.
        return False


def _report_unreadable(errors: list[str]) -> None:
    """Stream errors for skill directories that exist but cannot be read.

    The SDK shows skill load errors only to the model. The client shows these
    to the user, because the agent silently loses the skills they hold.
    """
    if not errors:
        return
    try:
        get_stream_writer()(skills_load_errors_event(errors))
    except Exception:
        # Best effort: a hook called outside a graph run has no stream.
        logger.debug("Could not stream skill load errors", exc_info=True)


def _skill_md_path(skill_dir: str) -> str:
    """Return the `SKILL.md` path inside a skill directory."""
    return str(PurePosixPath(to_posix_path(skill_dir)) / _SKILL_FILE)


def _namespace_skill(
    skill: sdk_skills.SkillMetadata,
    namespace: SkillNamespace,
    subfolders: tuple[str, ...],
) -> sdk_skills.SkillMetadata:
    """Return a copy of `skill` with a namespace-qualified name."""
    return cast(
        "sdk_skills.SkillMetadata",
        {
            **skill,
            "name": namespaced_skill_name(namespace, skill["name"], subfolders),
        },
    )


def discover_skill_dirs(
    backend: BackendProtocol,
    source_path: str,
    *,
    errors: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]]:
    """Return `(skill_dir, subfolders)` pairs found under `source_path`.

    Walks the source tree, treating any directory that directly contains a
    `SKILL.md` as a skill directory (a recursion leaf, like a plugin walker).
    `subfolders` holds the directory names between the source
    root and the skill directory, excluding the skill directory's own name.
    A directory that cannot be listed adds a message to `errors`.

    Returns:
        Skill directories paired with their intermediate subfolder segments.
    """
    found: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
    # `path_segments` accumulates directory names from the source root down to
    # and including `current`. A skill directory's own name is dropped when
    # naming, since the skill's terminal identifier is its frontmatter name;
    # only the directories above it form the namespace segments.
    source_root = Path(source_path).resolve()
    visited: set[Path] = set()
    stack: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = [(str(source_root), ())]
    while stack:
        current, path_segments = stack.pop()
        try:
            resolved = Path(current).resolve()
        except OSError, RuntimeError:
            logger.warning("Could not resolve plugin skill directory %s", current)
            continue
        if not resolved.is_relative_to(source_root) or resolved in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(resolved)
        resolved_path = str(resolved)
        entries = _entries(backend.ls(resolved_path), resolved_path, errors)
        if _has_skill_file(entries, resolved_path):
            found.append((resolved_path, path_segments[:-1]))
            continue
        for name, path in _child_dirs(entries, resolved_path):
            stack.append((path, (*path_segments, name)))
    return found


async def adiscover_skill_dirs(
    backend: BackendProtocol,
    source_path: str,
    *,
    errors: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]]:
    """Async counterpart of `discover_skill_dirs`.

    Returns:
        Skill directories paired with their intermediate subfolder segments.
    """
    found: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
    source_root = await asyncio.to_thread(Path(source_path).resolve)
    visited: set[Path] = set()
    stack: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = [(str(source_root), ())]
    while stack:
        current, path_segments = stack.pop()
        try:
            resolved = await asyncio.to_thread(Path(current).resolve)
        except OSError, RuntimeError:
            logger.warning("Could not resolve plugin skill directory %s", current)
            continue
        if not resolved.is_relative_to(source_root) or resolved in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(resolved)
        resolved_path = str(resolved)
        entries = _entries(await backend.als(resolved_path), resolved_path, errors)
        if _has_skill_file(entries, resolved_path):
            found.append((resolved_path, path_segments[:-1]))
            continue
        for name, path in _child_dirs(entries, resolved_path):
            stack.append((path, (*path_segments, name)))
    return found


def load_namespaced_skills(
    backend: BackendProtocol,
    source_path: str,
    namespace: SkillNamespace,
    *,
    errors: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[sdk_skills.SkillMetadata]:
    """Load and namespace every skill found under a plugin source.

    Reads each discovered skill directory's `SKILL.md` directly, since the SDK
    loader only scans one level below a source and would not read a leaf
    directory's own `SKILL.md`. Nested directories become `:`-joined namespace
    segments (e.g. `plugin:foo:bar:review`). A directory that cannot be listed
    adds a message to `errors`.

    Returns:
        Namespace-qualified skill metadata for the source.
    """
    skill_dirs = discover_skill_dirs(backend, source_path, errors=errors)
    if not skill_dirs:
        return []
    paths = [_skill_md_path(skill_dir) for skill_dir, _ in skill_dirs]
    responses = backend.download_files(paths)
    skills: list[sdk_skills.SkillMetadata] = []
    for (skill_dir, segments), path, response in zip(
        skill_dirs, paths, responses, strict=True
    ):
        skill = sdk_skills._skill_metadata_from_response(response, skill_dir, path)
        if skill is not None:
            skills.append(_namespace_skill(skill, namespace, segments))
    return skills


async def aload_namespaced_skills(
    backend: BackendProtocol,
    source_path: str,
    namespace: SkillNamespace,
    *,
    errors: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[sdk_skills.SkillMetadata]:
    """Async counterpart of `load_namespaced_skills`.

    Returns:
        Namespace-qualified skill metadata for the source.
    """
    skill_dirs = await adiscover_skill_dirs(backend, source_path, errors=errors)
    if not skill_dirs:
        return []
    paths = [_skill_md_path(skill_dir) for skill_dir, _ in skill_dirs]
    responses = await backend.adownload_files(paths)
    skills: list[sdk_skills.SkillMetadata] = []
    for (skill_dir, segments), path, response in zip(
        skill_dirs, paths, responses, strict=True
    ):
        skill = sdk_skills._skill_metadata_from_response(response, skill_dir, path)
        if skill is not None:
            skills.append(_namespace_skill(skill, namespace, segments))
    return skills


class PluginSkillsMiddleware(SkillsMiddleware):
    """Load namespaced plugin skills without extending the SDK source API.

    Wraps the SDK `SkillsMiddleware`. Sources without a namespace load exactly
    as the SDK loads them. Sources carrying a plugin namespace are walked
    recursively so nested skill directories (`skills/foo/bar/review/SKILL.md`)
    are discovered, and each skill's name is qualified as
    `plugin_id:foo:bar:review` before the last-one-wins merge — matching
    the plugin skill naming convention.
    """

    state_schema = _PluginSkillsState

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        backend: BackendProtocol,
        sources: Sequence[CodeSkillSource],
        system_prompt: str | None = sdk_skills.SKILLS_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        path_base: Path | None = None,
        tools: Sequence[BaseTool] = (),
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the middleware with Code-local plugin source tuples.

        Args:
            backend: Backend used to load skill files.
            sources: Ordered Code skill sources, optionally including a plugin
                namespace as the third tuple item.
            system_prompt: Skills prompt template passed to the SDK middleware.
            path_base: Directory that relative `skills.extra_allowed_dirs`
                entries resolve against. If `None`, the process working
                directory is used.
            tools: Tools disclosed only after their skill is read or pinned.
        """
        self._allowed_roots = tuple(Path(source[0]).resolve() for source in sources)
        self._path_base = path_base
        sdk_sources = [(source[0], source[1]) for source in sources]
        super().__init__(
            backend=backend,
            sources=sdk_sources,
            system_prompt=system_prompt,
            tools=tools,
        )
        self._namespaces = tuple(
            source[2] if len(source) == _PLUGIN_SKILL_SOURCE_LENGTH else None
            for source in sources
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _read_skill(skill: sdk_skills.SkillMetadata, roots: Sequence[Path]) -> str:
        """Return the selected skill's `SKILL.md` read within trusted roots.

        A skill outside every root interrupts the run to ask the user to trust
        its directory. An approval is saved, because later turns read trust
        only from the saved store.

        Errors are raised as `ValueError` because the agent server replaces the
        message of most other exception types, including `PermissionError`,
        before it reaches the client.

        Raises:
            ValueError: No trusted roots exist, the user denied trust, the
                approval could not be saved, or the file is unreadable.
        """
        name = skill["name"]
        # `load_skill_content` skips containment when given no roots, so an
        # empty list must fail here rather than read an unchecked path.
        if not roots:
            msg = f"Skill '{name}' cannot run: no trusted skill directories exist."
            raise ValueError(msg)
        try:
            content = load_skill_content(skill["path"], allowed_roots=roots)
        except PermissionError as exc:
            directory = _trusted_directory(skill, str(exc))
            try:
                content = load_skill_content(
                    skill["path"], allowed_roots=[*roots, Path(directory)]
                )
            except PermissionError as retry_exc:
                msg = (
                    f"Skill '{name}' changed location after you approved it, "
                    "so it was not read."
                )
                raise ValueError(msg) from retry_exc
        if content is None:
            msg = (
                f"Could not read instructions for skill '{name}'. Check that "
                "its SKILL.md exists, is UTF-8, and is not too large."
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        return content

    def before_model(
        self, state: sdk_skills.SkillsState, runtime: Runtime
    ) -> dict[str, object] | None:
        """Return SDK pin updates after validating skill selection and trust.

        Returns:
            An update that appends one pinned-skill message per requested name
                and clears `pinned_skills`, or `None` when nothing is pending.

        Raises:
            ValueError: A requested skill is missing on the server, or fails
                the trust or content checks.
        """
        del runtime
        names = state.get("pinned_skills")
        if not names:
            return None
        by_name = {skill["name"]: skill for skill in state.get("skills_metadata") or []}
        roots = [*self._allowed_roots, *extra_skill_roots(self._path_base)]
        messages: list[HumanMessage] = []
        for name in dict.fromkeys(names):
            if name not in by_name:
                msg = (
                    f"Skill '{name}' was not found. Check the name, or run "
                    "/reload if you just added it."
                )
                raise ValueError(msg)
            skill = by_name[name]
            body = pinned_skill_body(skill, self._read_skill(skill, roots))
            messages.append(sdk_skills._pinned_skill_message(skill, body))
        return {"pinned_skills": Overwrite([]), "messages": messages}

    async def abefore_model(
        self, state: sdk_skills.SkillsState, runtime: Runtime
    ) -> dict[str, object] | None:
        """Return trust-checked pin updates without blocking the event loop."""
        return await asyncio.to_thread(self.before_model, state, runtime)

    @staticmethod
    def _state_update(
        all_skills: dict[str, sdk_skills.SkillMetadata],
        errors: list[str],
        unreadable: list[str],
        state: sdk_skills.SkillsState,
    ) -> _SkillsStateUpdate:
        """Build the middleware state update, logging any load errors.

        Args:
            all_skills: Merged skill metadata keyed by name.
            errors: Every source error, shown to the model.
            unreadable: Errors for sources that exist, also shown to the user.
            state: State whose pending pins are trimmed.

        Returns:
            The state update carrying merged skill metadata and any errors.
        """
        # Always write the errors so warnings from an earlier load are cleared.
        update = _SkillsStateUpdate(
            skills_metadata=list(all_skills.values()),
            skills_load_errors=errors,
            skills_loaded_by=_PROCESS_ID,
        )
        if (pins := _pending_pin_update(state)) is not None:
            update["pinned_skills"] = pins
        if errors:
            logger.warning("Skills load errors: %s", errors)
        _report_unreadable(unreadable)
        return update

    def _load_source(
        self, source_path: str, namespace: SkillNamespace | None
    ) -> tuple[list[sdk_skills.SkillMetadata], list[str]]:
        """Return one source's skills and the errors from listing it."""
        if namespace is None:
            skills, error = sdk_skills._list_skills_with_errors(
                self._backend, source_path
            )
            return skills, [] if error is None else [error]
        errors: list[str] = []
        skills = load_namespaced_skills(
            self._backend, source_path, namespace, errors=errors
        )
        return skills, errors

    async def _aload_source(
        self, source_path: str, namespace: SkillNamespace | None
    ) -> tuple[list[sdk_skills.SkillMetadata], list[str]]:
        """Async counterpart of `_load_source`.

        Returns:
            The source's skills and the errors from listing it.
        """
        if namespace is None:
            skills, error = await sdk_skills._alist_skills_with_errors(
                self._backend, source_path
            )
            return skills, [] if error is None else [error]
        errors: list[str] = []
        skills = await aload_namespaced_skills(
            self._backend, source_path, namespace, errors=errors
        )
        return skills, errors

    def before_agent(
        self,
        state: sdk_skills.SkillsState,
        runtime: Runtime,  # noqa: ARG002
        config: RunnableConfig,  # noqa: ARG002
    ) -> sdk_skills.SkillsStateUpdate | None:
        """Load and namespace plugin skills before collision resolution.

        Returns:
            A state update containing collision-safe skill metadata and the
                trimmed `pinned_skills`, or `None` when the loaded skills serve
                the turn unchanged.
        """
        if not _needs_load(state):
            return _loaded_update(state)

        all_skills: dict[str, sdk_skills.SkillMetadata] = {}
        merged_source_labels: dict[str, str | None] = {}
        errors: list[str] = []
        unreadable: list[str] = []

        # `self.sources`, `self.source_labels`, and `self._namespaces` are all
        # built from the same source sequence at the same indices (see
        # `__init__` and the SDK base), so this zip is aligned by construction.
        # `strict=True` turns future *length* drift into a loud error; it does
        # not catch a same-length reorder, which would still mispair silently.
        for source_path, source_label, namespace in zip(
            self.sources, self.source_labels, self._namespaces, strict=True
        ):
            source_skills, source_errors = self._load_source(source_path, namespace)
            errors.extend(source_errors)
            # Optional skill directories often do not exist; that is not news.
            if source_errors and not _missing(source_path):
                unreadable.extend(source_errors)
            for skill in source_skills:
                merge_skill(
                    all_skills,
                    merged_source_labels,
                    skill,
                    source_label=source_label,
                )

        return self._state_update(all_skills, errors, unreadable, state)

    async def abefore_agent(
        self,
        state: sdk_skills.SkillsState,
        runtime: Runtime,  # noqa: ARG002
        config: RunnableConfig,  # noqa: ARG002
    ) -> sdk_skills.SkillsStateUpdate | None:
        """Asynchronously load and namespace skills before collision resolution.

        Returns:
            A state update containing collision-safe skill metadata and the
                trimmed `pinned_skills`, or `None` when the loaded skills serve
                the turn unchanged.
        """
        if not await asyncio.to_thread(_needs_load, state):
            return _loaded_update(state)

        all_skills: dict[str, sdk_skills.SkillMetadata] = {}
        merged_source_labels: dict[str, str | None] = {}
        errors: list[str] = []
        unreadable: list[str] = []

        # See `before_agent`: the three sequences are index-aligned by
        # construction, and `strict=True` guards against future length drift.
        for source_path, source_label, namespace in zip(
            self.sources, self.source_labels, self._namespaces, strict=True
        ):
            source_skills, source_errors = await self._aload_source(
                source_path, namespace
            )
            errors.extend(source_errors)
            if source_errors and not await asyncio.to_thread(_missing, source_path):
                unreadable.extend(source_errors)
            for skill in source_skills:
                merge_skill(
                    all_skills,
                    merged_source_labels,
                    skill,
                    source_label=source_label,
                )

        return self._state_update(all_skills, errors, unreadable, state)

"""Plugin discovery, install, and enablement helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import shutil
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from functools import partial

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from deepagents_code.plugins.manifest import (

)
from deepagents_code.plugins.models import (

)
from deepagents_code.plugins.store import (

    ensure_marketplace_cache_dir,
    ensure_plugin_data_dir,
    get_primary_install_entry,

    load_available_plugin_updates,
    load_enabled_plugin_ids,
    load_installed_plugins,
    load_marketplace_records,
    plugin_data_dir,

    remove_marketplace_record,
    save_available_plugin_updates,

    uninstall_plugin as uninstall_plugin_record,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Callable, Collection, Sequence, Set as AbstractSet

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_reported_broken: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
"""Broken installs already shown to the user in this process."""

_reported_broken_lock = threading.Lock()


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def add_local_marketplace(path: str | Path) -> PluginMarketplace:
    """Add a local marketplace to dcode state.

    Args:
        path: Marketplace root directory.

    Returns:
        Parsed marketplace.
    """
    marketplace = load_marketplace(Path(path))
    save_marketplace_record(
        MarketplaceRecord(
            name=marketplace.name,
            source_type="directory",
            source=str(marketplace.root),
            install_location=str(marketplace.root),
        )
    )
    return marketplace


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def add_marketplace_source(raw: str) -> PluginMarketplace:
    """Add a marketplace from a pasted source string.

    Args:
        raw: GitHub shorthand, Git URL, marketplace JSON URL, file, or directory.

    Returns:
        Parsed marketplace.
    """
    source = parse_marketplace_source(raw)
    marketplace, location = materialize_marketplace_source(source)
    save_marketplace_record(
        MarketplaceRecord(
            name=marketplace.name,
            source_type=source.source_type,
            source=source.value,
            install_location=str(location),
            ref=source.ref if isinstance(source, RepositoryMarketplaceSource) else None,
        )
    )
    return marketplace


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def remove_marketplace(name: str) -> bool:
    """Remove a marketplace and every plugin installed from it.

    Local marketplace source directories are never deleted. Managed marketplace
    clones and installed plugin caches are removed.

    Args:
        name: Marketplace name.

    Returns:
        `True` when a configured marketplace was removed.
    """
    record = load_marketplace_records().get(name)
    if record is None:
        return False

    installed = load_installed_plugins(strict=True)
    enabled = load_enabled_plugin_ids(strict=True)
    plugin_ids = set(installed) | set(enabled)
    for plugin_id in plugin_ids:
        try:
            _plugin_name, marketplace_name = split_plugin_id(plugin_id)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if marketplace_name == name:
            uninstall_plugin(plugin_id)

    removed = remove_marketplace_record(name)
    location = Path(record.install_location)
    try:
        resolved = location.resolve()
        cache_root = ensure_marketplace_cache_dir().resolve()
    except OSError:
        return removed
    if record.source_type in {"github", "git", "url"} and resolved.is_relative_to(
        cache_root
    ):
        if resolved.is_dir():
            shutil.rmtree(resolved, ignore_errors=True)
        elif resolved.is_file():
            resolved.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return removed


def _require_installed_plugin(plugin_id: str) -> None:
    """Raise when `plugin_id` does not identify an installed plugin.

    Raises:
        MarketplaceError: If the plugin is not installed.
    """
    if plugin_id not in load_installed_plugins(strict=True):
        msg = f"Plugin {plugin_id!r} is not installed"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def set_installed_plugin_enabled(plugin_id: str, *, enabled: bool) -> None:
    """Set the enabled state of an installed plugin.

    Args:
        plugin_id: Plugin id in `{name}@{marketplace}` form.
        enabled: Whether to enable the plugin.
    """
    _require_installed_plugin(plugin_id)
    set_plugin_enabled(plugin_id, enabled)
    if enabled:
        ensure_plugin_data_dir(plugin_id)


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def uninstall_plugin(plugin_id: str) -> None:
    """Uninstall a plugin (disable, clear records, delete orphaned cache).

    Args:
        plugin_id: Plugin id in `{name}@{marketplace}` form.
    """
    uninstall_plugin_record(plugin_id)


def _remote_marketplace_source(record: MarketplaceRecord) -> MarketplaceSource | None:
    """Rebuild the remote source for a persisted marketplace record.

    Returns:
        The repository or URL source, or `None` for local marketplaces.
    """
    match record.source_type:
        case "github" | "git":
            return RepositoryMarketplaceSource(
                source_type=record.source_type, value=record.source, ref=record.ref
            )
        case "url":
            return UrlMarketplaceSource(source_type="url", value=record.source)
        case _:
            return None


def load_record_marketplace(
    record: MarketplaceRecord, *, refresh_missing: bool = False
) -> PluginMarketplace:
    """Load a cached catalog, fetching the default on first browse.

    Returns:
        Parsed marketplace.

    Raises:
        MarketplaceError: If fetching is blocked by offline mode or a plugin mutation.
    """
    location = Path(record.install_location)
    refresh_missing = refresh_missing or (
        record.name == "langchain-plugins"
        and record.source_type == "github"
        and record.source == "langchain-ai/langchain-plugins"
    )
    source = _remote_marketplace_source(record) if refresh_missing else None
    if source is not None and not location.exists():
        from deepagents_code._env_vars import OFFLINE, is_env_truthy

        if is_env_truthy(OFFLINE):
            msg = f"Marketplace {record.name!r} is not cached; connect to browse it"
            raise MarketplaceError(msg)
        from filelock import Timeout

        try:
            with plugin_mutation_lock(timeout=0):
                if location.exists():
                    return load_marketplace_location(location)
                marketplace, location = materialize_marketplace_source(source)
                save_marketplace_record(replace(record, install_location=str(location)))
                return marketplace
        except Timeout as exc:
            msg = (
                "Another plugin operation is in progress; "
                "retry browsing when it finishes"
            )
            raise MarketplaceError(msg) from exc
    return load_marketplace_location(location)


def _resolve_marketplace_and_entry(
    plugin_id: str,
    *,
    refresh_missing: bool = False,
) -> tuple[PluginMarketplace, MarketplacePluginEntry]:
    try:
        plugin_name, marketplace_name = split_plugin_id(plugin_id)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise MarketplaceError(str(exc)) from exc
    records = load_marketplace_records()
    record = records.get(marketplace_name)
    if record is None:
        msg = f"Marketplace {marketplace_name!r} is not configured"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    marketplace = load_record_marketplace(record, refresh_missing=refresh_missing)
    entry = next(
        (plugin for plugin in marketplace.plugins if plugin.name == plugin_name),
        None,
    )
    if entry is None:
        msg = f"Plugin {plugin_id!r} not found in marketplace {marketplace_name}"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    return marketplace, entry


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def install_plugin(plugin_id: str) -> PluginInstance:
    """Install a marketplace plugin into the versioned cache and enable it.

    Copies the plugin source into `plugins/cache/{marketplace}/{plugin}/{version}/`,
    writes `installed_plugins.json`, and enables the plugin.

    Args:
        plugin_id: Plugin id in `{name}@{marketplace}` form.

    Returns:
        Discovered plugin instance loaded from the cache path.

    Raises:
        MarketplaceError: If the marketplace/plugin cannot be resolved, the
            source is unsupported, or the cached plugin fails to load.
    """
    installed = load_installed_plugins(strict=True)
    load_enabled_plugin_ids(strict=True)
    marketplace, entry = _resolve_marketplace_and_entry(plugin_id)
    existing = installed.get(plugin_id)
    cache_path = _copy_plugin_to_cache(
        plugin_id,
        marketplace,
        entry,
        refresh=existing is not None and not install_path_exists(existing.install_path),
    )

    set_plugin_enabled(plugin_id, True)
    ensure_plugin_data_dir(plugin_id)

    instance, warnings = _plugin_from_install_path(
        plugin_id=plugin_id,
        root=cache_path,
        marketplace_name=marketplace.name,
        fallback_name=entry.name,
    )
    if instance is None:
        detail = "; ".join(warnings)
        uninstall_plugin_record(plugin_id)
        msg = f"Installed {plugin_id} but failed to load from cache: {detail}"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    return instance


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def reinstall_plugin(plugin_id: str) -> PluginInstance:
    """Restore an installed plugin's files from its marketplace source.

    Unlike `install_plugin`, this always replaces the cached copy, even when the
    registry already lists the same version, so it repairs missing or damaged
    files. The enabled state and the plugin's data directory are left as-is.

    Args:
        plugin_id: Plugin id in `{name}@{marketplace}` form.

    Returns:
        Plugin instance loaded from the refreshed cache path.

    Raises:
        MarketplaceError: If the plugin is not installed, its source cannot be
            resolved, or the refreshed copy fails to load.
    """
    _require_installed_plugin(plugin_id)
    load_enabled_plugin_ids(strict=True)
    marketplace, entry = _resolve_marketplace_and_entry(plugin_id, refresh_missing=True)
    cache_path = _copy_plugin_to_cache(plugin_id, marketplace, entry, refresh=True)
    instance, warnings = _plugin_from_install_path(
        plugin_id=plugin_id,
        root=cache_path,
        marketplace_name=marketplace.name,
        fallback_name=entry.name,
    )
    if instance is None:
        msg = f"Reinstalled {plugin_id} but failed to load it: {'; '.join(warnings)}"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    with _reported_broken_lock:
        _reported_broken.difference_update(
            key for key in tuple(_reported_broken) if key[0] == plugin_id
        )
    return instance


def _copy_plugin_to_cache(
    plugin_id: str,
    marketplace: PluginMarketplace,
    entry: MarketplacePluginEntry,
    *,
    refresh: bool,
) -> Path:
    """Materialize a plugin source, copy it into the cache, and register it.

    Returns:
        Absolute path to the cached plugin root.

    Raises:
        MarketplaceError: If the source cannot be resolved or its manifest is
            invalid.
    """
    rejections: list[str] = []
    source_root = materialize_plugin_source(marketplace, entry, rejections=rejections)
    if source_root is None:
        raise MarketplaceError(unresolved_source_message(plugin_id, entry, rejections))
    try:
        manifest, _manifest_path, manifest_warnings = load_manifest(
            source_root, fallback_name=entry.name
        )
    except PluginManifestError as exc:
        msg = f"Cannot install {plugin_id}: {exc}"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg) from exc
    for warning in manifest_warnings:
        logger.debug("Plugin install warning for %s: %s", plugin_id, warning)
    return cache_and_register_plugin(
        plugin_id,
        source_root,
        version=manifest.version if manifest is not None else None,
        validate=partial(
            _validate_plugin_copy, plugin_id=plugin_id, fallback_name=entry.name
        ),
        refresh=refresh,
    )


def _validate_plugin_copy(
    root: Path,
    *,
    plugin_id: str,
    fallback_name: str,
) -> None:
    try:
        manifest, _manifest_path, warnings = load_manifest(
            root, fallback_name=fallback_name
        )
    except PluginManifestError as exc:
        msg = f"Cannot install {plugin_id}: {exc}"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg) from exc
    build_inventory(root, manifest, warnings)


def _plugin_from_install_path(
    *,
    plugin_id: str,
    root: Path,
    marketplace_name: str,
    fallback_name: str,
) -> tuple[PluginInstance | None, tuple[str, ...]]:
    warnings: list[str] = []
    try:
        manifest, _manifest_path, manifest_warnings = load_manifest(
            root, fallback_name=fallback_name
        )
    except PluginManifestError as exc:
        return None, (f"Skipping plugin {plugin_id}: {exc}",)
    warnings.extend(manifest_warnings)
    name = manifest.name if manifest and manifest.name else fallback_name
    inventory = build_inventory(root, manifest, tuple(warnings))
    try:
        instance = PluginInstance(
            plugin_id=plugin_id,
            name=name,
            marketplace=marketplace_name,
            version=manifest.version if manifest is not None else None,
            root=root,
            data_dir=plugin_data_dir(plugin_id),
            manifest=manifest,
            inventory=inventory,
        )
    except ValueError as exc:
        return None, (f"Skipping plugin {plugin_id}: {exc}",)
    return instance, inventory.warnings


def plugin_auto_update_setting() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Resolve whether plugin auto-updates are enabled and from which source.

    Returns:
        The enabled state and its configuration source.
    """
    from deepagents_code.config_manifest import (
        _emit_ranked_diagnostics,
        _ranked_source,
        get_option,
    )
    from deepagents_code.configuration.resolver import get_config_resolver

    option = get_option("plugins.auto_update")
    if option is None:
        return True, "default"
    resolved = get_config_resolver().get(option)
    _emit_ranked_diagnostics(option, resolved)
    return bool(resolved.value), _ranked_source(resolved)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
class _PendingUpdate:
    plugin_id: str
    entry: MarketplacePluginEntry
    source_root: Path
    manifest: PluginManifest
    update: PluginUpdate


def _refresh_source(
    record: MarketplaceRecord, *, include_local: bool
) -> MarketplaceSource | None:
    match record.source_type:
        case "directory" | "file" if include_local:
            return LocalMarketplaceSource(
                source_type=record.source_type, value=record.source
            )
        case _:
            return _remote_marketplace_source(record)


def _refresh_marketplace(
    record: MarketplaceRecord, *, include_local: bool, errors: list[str]
) -> PluginMarketplace | None:
    source = _refresh_source(record, include_local=include_local)
    if source is None:
        return None
    try:
        marketplace, _ = materialize_marketplace_source(source)
        if marketplace.name != record.name:
            msg = (
                f"Marketplace {record.name!r} now declares the name "
                f"{marketplace.name!r}"
            )
            raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
        detail = redact_urls_in_text(str(exc))
        logger.warning(
            "Could not refresh plugin marketplace %s: %s", record.name, detail
        )
        errors.append(f"Could not refresh marketplace {record.name}: {detail}")
        return None
    return marketplace


def _pending_update(
    marketplace: PluginMarketplace, plugin_id: str, installed_version: str
) -> _PendingUpdate | None:
    plugin_name, _ = split_plugin_id(plugin_id)
    entry = next((p for p in marketplace.plugins if p.name == plugin_name), None)
    if entry is None:
        msg = f"Plugin {plugin_id!r} not found in marketplace {marketplace.name}"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    rejections: list[str] = []
    source_root = materialize_plugin_source(marketplace, entry, rejections=rejections)
    if source_root is None:
        raise MarketplaceError(unresolved_source_message(plugin_id, entry, rejections))
    manifest, _manifest_path, _warnings = load_manifest(
        source_root, fallback_name=entry.name
    )
    if (
        manifest is None
        or manifest.name != plugin_name
        or not manifest.version
        or manifest.version == installed_version
    ):
        return None
    update = PluginUpdate(
        plugin_id=plugin_id,
        installed_version=installed_version,
        available_version=manifest.version,
    )
    return _PendingUpdate(
        plugin_id=plugin_id,
        entry=entry,
        source_root=source_root,
        manifest=manifest,
        update=update,
    )


def _install_update(pending: _PendingUpdate) -> None:
    cache_and_register_plugin(
        pending.plugin_id,
        pending.source_root,
        version=pending.update.available_version,
        validate=partial(
            _validate_plugin_copy,
            plugin_id=pending.plugin_id,
            fallback_name=pending.entry.name,
        ),
    )


def _collect_updates(
    targets: AbstractSet[str],
    *,
    include_local: bool,
    refresh_all: bool,
    should_install: Callable[[PluginManifest], bool],
) -> tuple[PluginUpdateResult, frozenset[str]]:
    """Compare installed target plugins with their marketplaces.

    Unversioned plugins are skipped so the running session's shared cache is not
    replaced.

    Returns:
        Installed and available updates plus redacted per-source errors, and the
        plugin ids whose comparison completed.
    """
    records = load_marketplace_records(strict=True)
    installed = load_installed_plugins(strict=True)
    updated: list[PluginUpdate] = []
    available: list[PluginUpdate] = []
    errors: list[str] = []
    checked: set[str] = set()
    for name, record in sorted(records.items()):
        plugin_ids = [
            plugin_id
            for plugin_id in sorted(targets)
            if plugin_id.rpartition("@")[2] == name
            and plugin_id in installed
            and installed[plugin_id].version is not None
        ]
        if not plugin_ids and (
            not refresh_all
            or (
                record.name == "langchain-plugins"
                and not Path(record.install_location).exists()
            )
        ):
            continue
        marketplace = _refresh_marketplace(
            record, include_local=include_local, errors=errors
        )
        if marketplace is None:
            continue
        for plugin_id in plugin_ids:
            installed_version = installed[plugin_id].version or ""
            try:
                pending = _pending_update(marketplace, plugin_id, installed_version)
                checked.add(plugin_id)
                if pending is None:
                    continue
                if not should_install(pending.manifest):
                    available.append(pending.update)
                    continue
                _install_update(pending)
                updated.append(pending.update)
            except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
                detail = redact_urls_in_text(str(exc))
                logger.warning("Could not update plugin %s: %s", plugin_id, detail)
                errors.append(f"Could not update plugin {plugin_id}: {detail}")
    result = PluginUpdateResult(
        updated=tuple(updated), available=tuple(available), errors=tuple(errors)
    )
    return result, frozenset(checked)


def _record_available_updates(
    result: PluginUpdateResult, checked: AbstractSet[str]
) -> PluginUpdateResult:
    """Persist available updates and mark those no earlier check reported.

    Entries for plugins this check could not compare, such as after a failed
    marketplace refresh, are kept so they are not announced again later.

    Returns:
        `result` with `newly_available` filled in.
    """
    previous = load_available_plugin_updates()
    current = {
        plugin_id: version
        for plugin_id, version in previous.items()
        if plugin_id not in checked
    }
    current.update((u.plugin_id, u.available_version) for u in result.available)
    if current != previous:
        try:
            save_available_plugin_updates(current)
        except OSError:
            logger.warning("Could not save available plugin updates", exc_info=True)
    newly = tuple(
        u for u in result.available if previous.get(u.plugin_id) != u.available_version
    )
    return replace(result, newly_available=newly)


def available_updates_message(updates: Sequence[PluginUpdate]) -> str:
    """Build the notification announcing plugin updates that were not installed.

    Returns:
        One-line message pointing the user at `/plugins`.
    """
    from deepagents_code.config import get_glyphs

    if len(updates) == 1:
        update = updates[0]
        name = update.plugin_id.rsplit("@", 1)[0]
        arrow = get_glyphs().arrow_right
        return (
            f"Plugin update available: {name} {update.installed_version} {arrow} "
            f"{update.available_version}. Open /plugins to update."
        )
    return f"Updates available for {len(updates)} plugins. Open /plugins to update."


def check_plugin_updates() -> PluginUpdateResult:
    """Refresh remote marketplaces and update enabled, opted-in plugins.

    Plugins whose manifest opts into `autoUpdate` are installed; other plugins
    with a different marketplace version are reported as available.

    Returns:
        Update outcome; empty when offline, disabled, or another mutation is
        in progress.
    """
    from filelock import Timeout

    from deepagents_code._env_vars import OFFLINE, is_env_truthy

    if is_env_truthy(OFFLINE) or not plugin_auto_update_setting()[0]:
        return PluginUpdateResult()
    try:
        with plugin_mutation_lock(timeout=0):
            result, checked = _collect_updates(
                load_enabled_plugin_ids(strict=True),
                include_local=False,
                refresh_all=True,
                should_install=lambda manifest: manifest.auto_update,
            )
            return _record_available_updates(result, checked)
    except Timeout:
        logger.debug(
            "Skipping plugin update check because another mutation holds the lock"
        )
        return PluginUpdateResult()


@plugin_mutation_lock()
def update_plugins(
    plugin_ids: Collection[str] = (), *, check_only: bool = False
) -> PluginUpdateResult:
    """Update installed plugins to their marketplace versions.

    Args:
        plugin_ids: Plugins to update; every installed plugin when empty.
        check_only: Report available updates without installing them.

    Returns:
        Update outcome.

    Raises:
        MarketplaceError: If a requested plugin is not installed.
    """
    installed = load_installed_plugins(strict=True)
    targets = frozenset(plugin_ids) or frozenset(installed)
    missing = sorted(targets - installed.keys())
    if missing:
        msg = f"Plugin {missing[0]!r} is not installed"
        raise MarketplaceError(msg)
    result, _checked = _collect_updates(
        targets,
        include_local=True,
        refresh_all=False,
        should_install=lambda _manifest: not check_only,
    )
    if result.updated:
        remaining = load_available_plugin_updates()
        for update in result.updated:
            remaining.pop(update.plugin_id, None)
        save_available_plugin_updates(remaining)
    return result


def discover_plugins() -> PluginDiscoveryResult:
    """Discover enabled marketplace plugins from their install cache paths.

    Returns:
        Discovery result. Broken marketplaces/plugins are returned as warnings and
        never abort sibling plugin loading.
    """
    enabled = load_enabled_plugin_ids()
    plugins: list[PluginInstance] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []
    broken: list[BrokenPluginInstall] = []

    for plugin_id in sorted(enabled):
        try:
            plugin_name, marketplace_name = split_plugin_id(plugin_id)
        except ValueError:
            warnings.append(f"Ignoring invalid plugin id {plugin_id!r}")
            continue
        entry = get_primary_install_entry(plugin_id)
        if entry is None:
            warnings.append(
                f"Plugin {plugin_id} is enabled but not installed "
                "(missing installed_plugins.json entry); run install to fix this"
            )
            continue
        root = Path(entry.install_path)
        try:
            root_exists = root.is_dir()
        except (OSError, RuntimeError) as exc:
            warnings.append(f"Plugin {plugin_id} cache could not be inspected: {exc}")
            continue
        if not root_exists:
            logger.debug(
                "Plugin %s is enabled but its install path %s is not a directory",
                plugin_id,
                entry.install_path,
            )
            broken.append(
                BrokenPluginInstall(
                    plugin_id=plugin_id, install_path=entry.install_path
                )
            )
            continue
        try:
            plugin, plugin_warnings = _plugin_from_install_path(
                plugin_id=plugin_id,
                root=root,
                marketplace_name=marketplace_name,
                fallback_name=plugin_name,
            )
        except (OSError, RuntimeError) as exc:
            warnings.append(f"Skipping plugin {plugin_id}: {exc}")
            continue
        warnings.extend(plugin_warnings)
        if plugin is not None:
            plugins.append(plugin)

    return PluginDiscoveryResult(
        plugins=tuple(plugins), warnings=tuple(warnings), broken=tuple(broken)
    )


def claim_broken_install_notices(
    broken: tuple[BrokenPluginInstall, ...],
) -> tuple[BrokenPluginInstall, ...]:
    """Return broken installs that have not yet been shown in this process.

    Several consumers (skills, hooks, MCP, the plugin manager) run discovery
    independently. Routing user-facing notices through this claim keeps each
    broken install to one warning per process while leaving other discovery
    warnings untouched. A successful `reinstall_plugin` releases the claim.

    Args:
        broken: Broken installs from a discovery result.

    Returns:
        The subset not previously claimed, in input order.
    """
    with _reported_broken_lock:
        fresh = tuple(
            item
            for item in broken
            if (item.plugin_id, item.install_path) not in _reported_broken
        )
        _reported_broken.update((item.plugin_id, item.install_path) for item in fresh)
    return fresh


def list_available_plugins() -> tuple[tuple[str, str, bool], ...]:
    """List plugins from configured marketplaces.

    Returns:
        Tuples of `(plugin_id, description, enabled)`.
    """
    records = load_marketplace_records()
    enabled = load_enabled_plugin_ids()
    rows: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
    for name, record in sorted(records.items()):
        try:
            marketplace = load_record_marketplace(record)
        except MarketplaceError as exc:
            rows.append((f"<marketplace:{name}>", str(exc), False))
            continue
        for plugin in marketplace.plugins:
            plugin_id = f"{plugin.name}@{marketplace.name}"
            rows.append((plugin_id, plugin.description or "", plugin_id in enabled))
    return tuple(rows)


def list_installed_plugin_ids() -> frozenset[str]:
    """Return plugin ids that have install records.

    Returns:
        Set of installed plugin ids.
    """
    return frozenset(load_installed_plugins())
